skill.name: competitor-profiling
skill.description: Research competitor websites, SEO signals, reviews, pricing, positioning, and customer proof from competitor URLs. Produces sourced competitor profile files and a cross-competitor summary.
skill.summary: Build sourced competitor profiles from URLs using site scraping, SEO data, review research, and structured markdown outputs.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

content.value_statement: Competitor research is slow when teams collect pages, SEO data, reviews, and pricing by hand. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to produce consistent competitor profiles.
actual_capabilities: Checks product marketing context before asking follow-up questions.
Uses Firecrawl map, scrape, and search workflows for competitor websites and reviews.
Uses DataForSEO MCP tools for backlinks, ranked keywords, traffic, and domain metrics.
Saves raw scrape, SEO, and review data in dated source folders.
Generates one markdown profile per competitor plus a comparison summary.
Supports quick scans, deep profiles, and profile updates with change logs.
limitations: Requires competitor URLs and enabled external MCP tools for live research.
Data quality depends on public websites, review sources, and SEO provider coverage.
Third-party scraping and SEO calls may add cost or hit provider limits.
Private customer claims cannot be verified without supporting public sources.

use_cases.title: Compare market positioning
use_cases.description: Build comparable profiles that show competitor messaging, pricing, customer proof, and strategic gaps.

use_cases.title: Validate a market entry
use_cases.description: Research direct competitors before choosing differentiation, pricing, or launch messaging.

use_cases.title: Prepare sales research
use_cases.description: Create sourced competitor dossiers that can feed battle cards, objection handling, and account planning.

prompt_templates.title: Quick competitor scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small set of competitors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile these competitor URLs: [urls]. Use quick scan mode and focus on positioning, pricing, and customer proof.

prompt_templates.title: Deep competitor profile
prompt_templates.scenario: Full research request for strategic planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build deep profiles for [competitors]. Include website scraping, review themes, SEO metrics, raw data folders, and a summary comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh an old profile
prompt_templates.scenario: Updating existing research without losing history.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update our existing [competitor] profile from [date]. Re-pull pricing, SEO metrics, changelog signals, and add a change log.

prompt_templates.title: Landscape gap analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced market mapping across many possible competitors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a competitive landscape report for [market]. Prioritize the top five relevant competitors and identify positioning gaps.

output_examples.input: Profile three competitors for sales enablement and positioning research.
output: Three sourced competitor profile documents with pricing, messaging, SEO signals, reviews, and strengths.
One summary document comparing key metrics, positioning, and opportunities.
Dated raw source folders for each competitor.

output_examples.input: Update a competitor profile that is four months old.
output: An updated profile with refreshed pricing, SEO metrics, changelog signals, and generated date.
A change log that explains what changed since the prior profile.
A new dated raw data folder that preserves the older snapshot.

output_examples.input: Skip SEO data and only research pricing, positioning, and customer logos.
output: An abbreviated profile focused on homepage messaging, pricing details, and customer proof.
A clear note that SEO metrics were not collected by request.
Saved raw page scrapes for later reuse.

best_practices: Confirm scope, depth, and focus areas before running expensive research.
Save raw source data with dates so claims can be audited later.
Label inferences clearly and cite the source behind each claim.
anti_patterns: Profiling many competitors deeply without prioritizing relevance.
Leaving unavailable SEO or pricing fields blank without explanation.
Treating homepage claims or logo walls as verified customer evidence.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs competitor URLs, your product context, desired depth, and any focus areas.

faq.question: Can it run without Firecrawl or DataForSEO?
faq.answer: It can outline research, but live scraping and SEO metrics require those tools.

faq.question: Does it create sales battle cards?
faq.answer: It creates profiles and summaries. Use a sales enablement workflow to convert profiles into battle cards.

faq.question: How does it handle many competitors?
faq.answer: It recommends prioritizing the top five and using quick scans for large lists.

faq.question: Can profiles be updated later?
faq.answer: Yes. It saves new dated raw data and adds a change log to updated profiles.

faq.question: Is confidential product data safe to include?
faq.answer: Provide only context needed for comparison. Review generated files before sharing them outside your workspace.
